The root cause was that do_become_nonbusy() relied solely on the runflags parameter to determine whether to free chanlist memory, but in exceptional exit paths where runflags was never set, the allocation wasn't freed. This commit fixes the issue by: (1) Adding a new COMEDI_SRF_BUSY flag that is explicitly set in do_cmd_ioctl() at line 1925 when the command is set up, (2) Modifying do_become_nonbusy() to check this flag via comedi_is_runflags_busy(runflags) at line 796 instead of relying on implicit runflags state, (3) Introducing reference counting with comedi_get_is_subdevice_running() and comedi_put_is_subdevice_running() to safely manage async command cleanup, and (4) Ensuring chanlist is freed at line 805 only when the COMEDI_SRF_BUSY flag was actually set, preventing the memory leak in exceptional exit paths. The code now explicitly tracks whether a command was set up via the COMEDI_SRF_BUSY flag, making the cleanup logic robust against all exit paths.
